conceptual.anchor: the variational lower bound can be monitored during iterative estimation and used to check convergence and software implementation correctness. ... Approximation -> Bound -> Monitor -> Validate. ... Variational inference is therefore not 'cheap AI'. It should be treated as controlled approximation with an explicit mathematical objective.

formal.anchor: This book does not merely validate our previous HMM/HSMM hybrid idea. It suggests a more general architecture: KnowledgeOS should have an adaptive inference fabric that selects among deterministic inference, HMM/HSMM, graphical-model inference, continuous-state filtering, variational approximation, sampling, and model ensembles.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Do not adopt from the book as an architectural authority: probability as a definition of truth; model output as knowledge; statistical confidence as governance authority; automatic model selection as sovereign architecture; dimensionality reduction without information-loss accounting. ... Don't build one powerful inference engine. Build a structured inference fabric that can cheaply solve easy problems, accurately solve difficult problems, abstain when the evidence is insufficient, and spend computational resources only where the expected epistemic/decision value justifies them.
rationale_evidence.statement: Final adopt/reject list (17 items adopted including inference/decision separation, reject/abstain/escalate, expected-loss computation, model evidence+complexity selection, graph factorization, LDS/particle filtering, variational assurance, ARD, mixture-of-experts, BMA, online inference, numerical stability, posterior preservation; 5 explicit non-adoptions including probability-as-truth and confidence-as-governance-authority) and the bottom-line architectural slogan for the whole EGAIF proposal.
